newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan finds new locations for nuclear waste.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan finds new locations for nuclear waste.

text.p: The state-run utility Taiwan Power Company (Taipower), facing increasing environmental protests, said on Wednesday it had found five potential sites to store nuclear waste.
Taipower said in a statement the five dump sites were in the offshore island of Matsu, the eastern counties of Hualien and Taitung, and in the southern county of Pingtung.
Taipower would make a final decision from the five candidates and the local government and residents at the winning site would receive a T$3 billion (US$109 million) reward, an official said.

"To appreciate their participation, Taipower will give T$50 million (US$1.8 million) each to local governments of the five qualified sites, and T$1 million ($36,000) thank-you money to four unqualified sites," a Taipower spokesman said.
The company would use part of its income from nuclear power generation to finance the reward, the spokesman said.
Taiwan decided last July to stop sending nuclear waste to tiny Lanyu island, its only nuclear waste dump, following strong protests by residents there.
Since 1982, Taiwan has stored 97,672 barrels of nuclear waste at the Lanyu dump, which has a capacity of 98,112 barrels.
Taipower has promised to remove all the nuclear waste from Lanyu by 2002 and it has been seeking sites overseas, including in China, the Marshall Islands and Russia.
"The plan to look for appropriate dumps overseas remains unchanged," the spokesman said.
Taiwan has three nuclear power plants and the government plans to build a fourth in the northern county of Taipei.

A deeply divided parliament battled over Taiwan's nuclear future for five months after opposition lawmakers last May managed to cancel funding for the fourth plant. The ruling party restored the plan in October.
But the state's victory angered opposition forces, who staged brief but fiery riots after the final vote in one of the worst outbreaks of political violence in a decade.
